profile.headline: Senior Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat
profile.summary:
Principal Engineer/Architect in a small and fast paced development environment while continuing to increase my level of responsibility.  I am interested in working in an adaptive development environment that utilizes many different languages and technologies to solve problems in the best possible way.

Specialties: Java, JSP, Java Servlets, C++, C, JavaScript, Smalltalk, XML, XQuery, XSLT, WSDL, Web Services, BPEL, HTML, SQL, Python, Windows, Linux, MS Visual Studio, Eclipse, J2EE, CVS, SSH, JUnit, Tomcat, XML, Soap, MySQL, SQL Server

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: Working as a project lead at Red Hat in the API Design space.

positions.title: Technical Lead
positions.description: Working as a technical lead in the Technology & Planning department of Yale University.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description: Active Endpoints creates technology around BPEL (Business Process Execution Language), which is a high level XML based language for managing business processes.  We create server technology for executing applications written in BPEL as well as Eclipse based tooling for writing BPEL applications.

positions.title: Senior Product Development Engineer
positions.description: Worked as a senior engineer on a J2EE "Telecommunications Cost Management" application.  The application helps companies reduce their telecommunications spend by importing billing data, managing inventory, and analyzing usage costs.  I was responsible for the Assurance subsystem, which was designed to analyze large amounts of billing data and report problems and/or abnormalities.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: Worked as a designer and implementer of both a Java based server product as well as a C++ based, Windows client application.  Mirror Worlds Technologies has two products, both based on a "time-centric" content management software paradigm envisioned by Yale professor David Gelertner.  The server is a groupware/collaborative product that allows multiple users to store, retrieve, and share documents through a web browser.  The client application is a utility that is installed on a single users Windows PC and allows the user to search for their "stuff".

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description: Worked as a software development summer intern doing/learning development in Smalltalk.

projects.title: Apicurio
projects.description: Apicurio is an open source community containing multiple projects largely related to APIs and schemas.  This includes, but is not limited to, a Designer and a Registry.

projects.title: Apiman project
projects.description: I am a core contributor to apiman, a fast, open source API Management platform
